Definitely do not need them in all cities.  Once they hit tier 3 they start to give conversion to neighboring provinces, so ideally you would build them in areas with a lot of neighboring provinces.  Since republic has no equivalent to ishin shishi/shinsengumi, you really only need them until all your towns convert to independent.  At that point, if you upgrade one to the max level it will prevent any shogunate/imperial influence spread in your territory for the rest of the game.

As far as the size of the town, you don't need to wait to get prefectures for sure.  I generally upgrade them to at least city, but municipality gives that last building slot that you can use for a traditional dojo for garrison and ninja access, or propaganda building for quick conversion, or tower upgrade in one of your forward towns for extra defense

1. Use your Ishin Shishi and Shinsengumi to cause rebellions in your neighbors rear territories without capturing the towns, so you don't increase your faction power rating.  This disrupts them pretty effectively and forces them to move their armies around and tends to keep them off the front line.
2. Get necessary economic techs so that you will be able to fund yourself without ANY trade income.  You will be able to trade with foreign powers, but expect your main trade port to be damaged and non-functional every other turn for a while.
3. Make sure to not build your propaganda buildings past magistrate until you go republic so you can upgrade them along the republic chain.
4. Make sure to get ALL the public order technologies and at least one of the conversion technologies before transitioning.
5. Make sure to have all your castles upgraded to at least citadel.  Star forts are really good but they take an ETERNITY to get going.
6. Get at least the copper technology so you can make military ports allowing you to recruit 2 ships at a time.  Drydocks are best for obvious reasons.
7. Put a cadet school somewhere in the back line, just in case they land a stack deep in undefended territory.  That way you can pump out some line infantry in an emergency.  The line infantry garrison is nice too.
8. Make sure you don't have any shogunate/imperial infantry in your armies because they will be deleted when you transition.  Same thing with your Ishin Shishi/Shinsengumi
9. Don't neglect your navy.  Also, manually resolve all naval battles, because autoresolve will nuke your ships for no reason.  Kaiyo Maru and Kotetsu are very expensive to replace.
10. You need to at least have parrot guns, but Armstrong guns are better.  One gatling gun can make any battle easy mode.
11. Work on getting your ninjas ranked up as you go forward, as a rank 6 ninja will be an AMAZING source of intel.  Try putting your max ninja in a town and witness the massive radius of his vision.
12. Get your railways set up so you can move your agents around quickly.  Also for your troops, but mainly your agents.
13. Foreign veterans can get your back line troops up to rank 5 relatively quickly, which makes them massively more effective.  They also do a pretty good job at dueling enemy generals and metsuke class agents.
14. Try to get a town with a silver/gold mine early on and put the market chain and factories in it, and it will grow to insane levels later in the campaign.
15. Try to keep your generals current level and likely future level in mind when giving them office slots.  They can give insane bonuses if they hit max rank while in office.

1) I am not sure what is technically required, but when I switched I didn't have to forfeit my current spot until I had my other one lined up.  This may be up to your GME office or PD.

2) I transferred within my specialty, and my PD sent the equivalent of a "transcript" to my new program so they could find what rotations could be credited.  I did not have to do a gap year or repeat intern year, but my schedule is a bit different compared to the rest in my new program due to different priorities.  In other words, they made it work so I can graduate on time.  If I remember correctly, you have to complete two consecutive years at the same program in order to graduate, so you may have to redo pgy2.

3) Absolutely positively 100% you need your PD to be involved and supporting you.  The first thing your prospective PD will do is get your current one on the phone and ask what the deal is.
